title: AASB 116 Property, Plant and Equipment — December 2022 compilation
use: Scoped recognition, direct costs, component depreciation, readiness, residual/life review and derecognition.
verification: Actual official HTML body inspected: paragraphs 6–20, 43, 48–62A and 67–70. Public issuer text incorporates IAS 16 with separately identified Australian additions. Used as a dated method reference, not a claim of current jurisdiction-wide compliance or a complete standard. 2025–2027 Alder dates follow explicitly frozen teaching conventions.

title: AASB 108 Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors — March 2021 compilation
use: New information versus error and prospective estimate revision.
verification: Actual official HTML paragraphs 32–40 read, including 34 new-information distinction and 36–38 prospective application. Does not establish a current filing policy or support treating an error as an estimate change.

title: AASB 136 Impairment of Assets — December 2022 compilation
use: Recoverable amount, independent cash-flow unit, subsequent depreciation and reversal ceiling.
verification: Official HTML inspected: definitions 6; 8–10, 18–22; 59–63; 109–121 and 124. Related cash-flow consistency, exclusions of financing/tax and discount-risk guidance in paragraphs 44–55 were read in the official January 2026 compilation PDF as additional method context, not used to claim universal current applicability. The chapter freezes a simple cost-model convention; excludes goodwill allocation and non-independent CGU valuation.

title: AASB 138 Intangible Assets — December 2022 compilation
use: Finite-life amortization; indefinite-life boundary; research/development recognition.
verification: Actual official HTML read: definition/identifiability/control 8–13; 48–57, 63–71; 88–100; 107–110. Six development conditions, date recognition starts, no reinstatement of earlier expense, readiness and legal/economic useful-life distinction inspected. Business-combination intangibles, goodwill and unusual revenue-based exceptions are not developed.

title: AASB 140 Investment Property — December 2022 compilation
use: Owned operating property versus rental/capital-appreciation property; fixed cost versus fair-value models.
verification: Actual official HTML paragraphs 5–9, 30–35, 53–57 read. Model-policy scope and exceptions inspected. Original example assumes an owned completed property with reliably measurable fair value, no special pools, no lease right-of-use asset and no transfer of use. No blanket claim that every framework permits fair-value gains in profit.

title: IFRS Foundation — IFRS 9 Financial Instruments public overview
use: Recognition and the business-model/contractual-cash-flow boundary for a supplied amortized-cost claim.
verification: Actual public About section read: recognition as party to contractual provisions, initial measurement, held-to-collect business model and solely-principal-and-interest condition for amortized cost. Full subscription standard was not accessed. The exact effective-interest schedule is independently derived from supplied cash flows and a stipulated qualifying, no-credit-loss case; no general fair-value/OCI classification or impairment measurement is inferred from the overview.

title: S. P. Kothari, MIT 15.511 — Long-lived Assets, 25 June 2004
use: Historical teaching reference for cost allocation, useful life/residual value, straight-line/usage methods and noncash depreciation.
verification: Actual 15-page lecture PDF inspected, particularly PDF pages 4–7 and 9–15. No source examples or numbers reproduced. The chapter does not import the slides’ broad R&D, land, US-method prevalence or tax statements as current universal rules. Modern classification boundaries use scoped official issuer text instead.
